<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **6** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/scenarios`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **49** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`, `packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/agent-ceiling-clamp.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 87af66e5b6c75af7989ecbdc8820f1ca4a66596a`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`, `packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/agent-ceiling-clamp.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **15** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **186** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 87af66e5b6c75af7989ecbdc8820f1ca4a66596a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `dd2d9ee1d06c7975e3858e497e8540b8925f3c22` — the merge of head `25e18d4cdb16f02bba83aee105073c9a2e46e56f` into base `87af66e5b6c75af7989ecbdc8820f1ca4a66596a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin dd2d9ee1d06c7975e3858e497e8540b8925f3c22 && git checkout dd2d9ee1d06c7975e3858e497e8540b8925f3c22
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 87af66e5b6c75af7989ecbdc8820f1ca4a66596a 25e18d4cdb16f02bba83aee105073c9a2e46e56f && git checkout -B drift-repro 87af66e5b6c75af7989ecbdc8820f1ca4a66596a && git merge --no-ff 25e18d4cdb16f02bba83aee105073c9a2e46e56f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 87af66e5b6c75af7989ecbdc8820f1ca4a66596a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 87af66e5b6c75af7989ecbdc8820f1ca4a66596a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bad558d574b997d7bc271793693fab55085331a4`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/conversions/entries/18/permission-modify-all-allow-delete-false-to-true.ts, packages/spec/src/conversions/entries/19/permission-view-all-fields-beside-record-bypass.ts, packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts, packages/spec/src/conversions/stored.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/19.permission-view-all-modify-all-cast-no-field-vote.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template, packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts + packages/core/src/security/effective-object-permissions.ts, packages/core/src/security/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/permission-evaluator.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/agent-ceiling-clamp.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/artifact-forward-conversion.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-rollup-source-visibility.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/score/scenario-tags.ts, packages/spec/liveness/permission.json

PR #37371 for card #36055. Inputs read: the card body and all 11 comments (rulings 7177220994 and 7177446075, claim 7177278985 with amendment 1, both dev reports), the PR body, the 54-path file list, the net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on this head. The remaining 35 paths (tests, docs, generated references, the showcase, the changeset) are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

Check-runs on the head, read once: 2 failure, the rest success or skipped, none pending (the second `Check Changeset` run completed success at 15:13Z).

- RED, and caused by this diff: `Lint · docs & code guards` (52 gates: 51 passed, 1 red) and its aggregate `Lint & Repo Gates`. The one red gate is `check:adr-symbol-anchors`, 1 finding: `docs/adr/0066-unified-authorization-model.md:146` anchors `effective-object-permissions.ts#superuserFieldVote`, the symbol this PR removes. The job log names nothing else. See ③ E1.
- Accept-set, `ObjectPermissionSchema`: unchanged. No key added or removed, no refinement changed; only JSDoc and `.describe()` text on `viewAllRecords`, `modifyAllRecords`, `viewAllFields` and the field-permission `when`. Right: the change is a meaning change, not a shape change, which is why it is a default flip and not a rename.
- Accept-set, conversions: `CONVERSIONS_BY_MAJOR[19]` now exists with one entry; `step19.conversionIds` derives from it, as step 18's do. Right. `check-adr-0087-registration`, `check:generated`, `check:upgrade-guide`, `check:spec-changes` and the retired-after census ran in the green lanes.
- Public surface removed: `@objectstack/core` `superuserFieldVote` (replaced by `viewAllFieldsReadVote(sets, objectName, fieldName): boolean`); `@objectstack/plugin-security` `ConditionedFieldEntry.supersededBy`; `@objectstack/lint` `SECURITY_SUPERUSER_FIELD_MASK_INERT`, the rule id, and the `bit` / `reopened` user-text params of `security-cross-set-field-reopen`. Each is right for a major. No reader of any of them is left in the tree outside tests and `CHANGELOG.md` history; `TypeScript Type Check`, `Type Check UI` and `Test Core` 10/10 are green.
- Behaviour: both field merges (`getFieldPermissions`, `buildEffectiveFieldPermissions`) ask one function. Right, and it is the card's acceptance.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes — the PR body and the changeset both carry `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: semantic`. The value starts with `yes`, which is what the card owes; the `(narrowing)` suffix is the dev's addition and the PR-body guards and `Check Changeset` pass on it.

The changeset matches what the diff publishes: `major` for `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/lint` and `@objectstack/spec` (removed exports and a changed meaning of two published keys), `minor` for `@objectstack/metadata-core` (the door refuses one more id). It names the conversion id in the ADR-0087 marker, the FROM → TO, the stored-set reading and the fix. `@objectstack/cli` and `@objectstack/service-automation` take a `patch` for test-comment edits only: not wrong, not needed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- E1 (escalated to the seat, not graded: `docs/adr/**` is outside this diff). The head is red on a gate this diff turns red, and the stated repair has an ordering problem. The PR body says the ADR PR of #37245 re-points the anchor to `#viewAllFieldsReadVote` "before this PR leaves draft". That symbol does not exist on `main` until this PR merges, so an ADR PR carrying it is red on `main` by the same gate; and this PR is red until the anchor moves. One of three has to be chosen: the ADR PR first re-points line 146 to a symbol both trees hold, this PR's claim is widened by that one line (the dev's earlier option B), or the two land together. Ruling 7177220994 routes the D2 ⑧ note to #37245 "after merge", which does not cover the anchor. This verdict is about the contract; it does not make the head landable.
- Dev open question 1 (interim report): no command lists affected STORED sets, and Studio has no `viewAllFields` control. Answered by the final report as option A: the predicate and the metadata-API fix are in the changeset and the D3 entry, the review list is follow-up #37375. Consistent with ruling 7177446075's execution note (a one-step check an operator can follow). I did not read #37375 or #37374; the seat confirms both exist before adopting.
- Dev open question 2: the ADR anchor. See E1.
- Dev flag, premise refinement: Modify All's cross-set EDIT re-open is lost, the built-in admin sets beside an app set's edit lock included. Inside ruling 6912661484 as the card quotes it (`viewAllFields` is read-only), named in the changeset and in the D3 entry. Accepted. The measured 12 edit cells in the showcase are this case.
- Published skills still teach that Modify All grants a field edit (`skills/**`, out of the claimed surface, carrier #37374). Until it lands, a skill contradicts the shipped contract; it should land in the same release.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The diff adds no id materialisation and no in-app join; the field merges read the caller's already-resolved permission sets, as before.

### ④ Design judgment

S1 (should-fix) — `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/19.permission-view-all-modify-all-cast-no-field-vote.ts`. The card says the one change the conversion cannot keep is "Modify All plus the same set's own `editable: false` / `readable: false` row", and that the entry names it. The entry names half of it and contradicts itself on the other half:
  - `acceptanceCriteria` says, for an entry with either bit, "add `viewAllFields: true`; nothing else is needed for the read". That is false for a Modify All set with its own `readable: false` row: `viewAllFieldsReadVote` skips a field the set's own row hides (`declaresOwnReadMask`), so after the bit is added, by hand or by the conversion, that field is hidden from the set's holders, where Modify All read it before. `reason` item (3) says so; the criteria, the text an operator verifies against, say the opposite. The changeset carries the qualifying sentence; the entry's criteria do not.
  - The same-set EDIT lock is not named. `reason` item (2) and the criteria speak only of "a field another set locks". A Modify All set whose own field row omits `editable: true` (an omitted `editable` is `false`) edited that field until 19 and no longer does, with no second set involved. `permission.zod.ts` says it ("a field this set's own row hides or locks"); the entry does not.
  Fix: state both own-row cases in the criteria with their remedy (delete the own `readable: false` row, or write `editable: true` on the own row), and drop or qualify "nothing else is needed for the read". The error direction is fewer fields, so this is not a must-fix; it is the upgrade contract for a security change, so it is not a nit.

No must-fix.

Nits, no effect on correctness:
- N1 (nit) — the same entry and the changeset say the authoring funnel refuses the conversion "by id". The funnel skips it through `retiredFromLoadPath` (`applyConversions`, `includeRetired` false); only the artifact door and the stored seam refuse by id. The conversion's own docblock has it right.
- N2 (nit, outside the diff, read not reviewed) — `packages/spec/src/identity/eval-user.zod.ts`, the comment on `ADMIN_FULL_ACCESS_CAPABILITIES` still says `viewAllFields` "duplicates the vote the two record bits already cast on every field". False at this head. A follow-up, or the fix round for S1 carries it.

What holds, file by file, against the code at this head:

- `entries/19/permission-view-all-fields-beside-record-bypass.ts`. The predicate (`viewAllRecords === true || modifyAllRecords === true`, `viewAllFields === undefined`, per `objects` entry, `'*'` included) writes the bit on exactly the entry that carried the old vote. `holdsSuperuserBypass` and `holdsViewAllFields` take the same lookup (`objects[name] || objects['*']`), so the new vote reaches the same objects the old one did, and no further: a set with a bypass `'*'` and an explicit bit-less entry for an object cast no vote on that object before and casts none after. I tried to make the conversion open a field and could not: for View All the old vote and the new vote are the same function of the same rows; for Modify All the new vote is a subset (read only, own `readable: false` rows excluded). Leaving an authored `viewAllFields: false` alone is right and makes the replay idempotent. `retiredFromLoadPath: true` with `retiredAfter: '18.6.0'` matches the type's rule for a stable label (`@objectstack/spec` is `18.6.0` in pre mode, not yet versioned) and the precedent `flow-decision-mode-inclusive-explicit`. The docblock's account of where it replays agrees with the three seams below.
- `registry.ts`. `MAJOR_19_CONVERSIONS` takes major 18's `{ conversion, order }` shape; the `inApplicationOrder` call carries the `@__PURE__` annotation the table's own warning demands.
- `stored.ts`. `STORED_ROWS_NOT_REWRITTEN` is spread first into `excludeConversionIds` and the caller's list is appended, so no caller can remove it; `applyConversions` reads the exclusion before the retirement window. Every stored-row caller in the tree goes through this function (database loader, ObjectQL plugin, metadata-protocol `convertStoredItemDetailed`, translation sync, datasource admin). This is ruling 7177446075, option A, as written.
- Other replay seams, read to find one the PR missed: the only `includeRetired: true` callers besides `stored.ts` are the artifact door and the two flow seams, and the flow seams pass a `flows`-only stack that a `permissions` walk never touches. `applyMetaMigrations` (by id, source only) is the single place the entry runs; `os migrate meta --stored` is exclusive with `--from` and goes through the stored seam. None missed.
- `artifact-forward-conversion.ts`. The id is in `DEFAULT_FLIPS_NOT_REPLAYED_HERE`, which is the exclusion for the undeclared and converted-forward verdicts and is seeded into `closed` (and skipped before either half can open it) in `idsTheFloorPostdates`. Refused in all four windows.
- `registry.ts.template`. `step19.conversionIds` derives from `CONVERSIONS_BY_MAJOR[19]`; the rationale sentence is accurate.
- `permission.zod.ts`. Each changed sentence agrees with `viewAllFieldsReadVote`: read vote only, never edit, own `readable: false` row beats the set's own bit, applied to the fields the merge names, View All and Modify All cast no vote. The `when` description's "a row-conditioned lock binds its holders" matches the explain change.
- `effective-object-permissions.ts`, `permission-evaluator.ts`. One vote function, asked per field by both merges; `holdsSuperuserBypass` is untouched and has no field reader left. I read every other reader of the two record bits in `packages/**` and `ui/**` at this head for a second field-axis reading (a mask skipped for a super-user): none; they are row, transfer, recycle-bin and posture readers.
- `explain-engine.ts`. Dropping the "superseded" branch is right: nothing can vote an edit over a conditioned lock any more.
- `validate-security-posture.ts`, `validate-rollup-source-visibility.ts`. `viewAllFieldsVoteOf` mirrors the core vote for one set; the cross-set rule now fires only on `readable: false` re-opened by another set's `viewAllFields`, which is what the D3 entry tells the operator `os validate` reports. The two skips "beside the set's own Modify All" are removed, consistent with own rows binding.
- `default-permission-sets.ts`, `agent-ceiling-clamp.ts`, `scenario-tags.ts`, `liveness/permission.json`: comments, evidence anchor and one scoring reader moved to the new reading; each agrees with the code.

Delta review of PR #37371 for card #36055, on top of record 7196108575 (PASS on `bad558d574b997d7bc271793693fab55085331a4`). Read: the diff `bad558d574..71a5990508` (2 commits, 4 files, +29 −17), the four changed files whole at this head, the code they describe, the 55-path file list and the check-runs on this head. The file list grew by one path, `packages/spec/src/identity/eval-user.zod.ts`; it is a governed path, so `hits` is 8 paths, one more than the previous record. The other 35 paths stay the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

Nothing that runs changed since `bad558d574`. The delta is: prose in the changeset; a docblock bullet in the conversion entry; `//` comment lines in `eval-user.zod.ts` (the `ADMIN_FULL_ACCESS_CAPABILITIES` value is untouched); and the `replacement`, `reason` and `acceptanceCriteria` strings of the protocol-19 semantic entry (`id`, `surface` and `conversionIds` untouched). No accept-set, export, predicate or seam moved, so ①, ②, ③ and the file-by-file reading of 7196108575 stand for this head.

Check-runs on this head, read once after the last one completed: 74 runs, none pending. 59 success, 12 skipped, 1 cancelled, 2 failure.

- The cancelled run is the first `PR-body guards` run, superseded; its re-run is success.
- RED: `Lint · docs & code guards` (52 gates: 51 passed, 1 red, 0 did not run) and its aggregate `Lint & Repo Gates` (red on that one lane; every other lint lane success). The red gate is `check:adr-symbol-anchors`, 1 finding across 163 records: `docs/adr/0066-unified-authorization-model.md:146` anchors `packages/core/src/security/effective-object-permissions.ts#superuserFieldVote`, the symbol this PR removes. The job log carries no other finding. Same red as on the previous head; see ③ E1.
- Green on the new text: both `Check Changeset` runs, `Test Core` 10/10 and its aggregate, `Test UI` 16/16, all five type-check runs, `Spec property liveness`, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes — unchanged: the PR body and the changeset still carry `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: semantic`; the bump table of the changeset is untouched by the delta.

### ③ Boundary flags

- E1 (escalated, not graded; open as in 7196108575). The head is still red on `check:adr-symbol-anchors` at ADR-0066:146. `docs/adr/**` is outside this diff and the anchor is carried by the ADR PR of card #37245. The ordering problem named in 7196108575 is not changed by this delta: the seat chooses the order in which the two land. This verdict is about the contract; it does not make the head landable.
- The other flags of 7196108575 (follow-ups #37375 and #37374, the Modify All edit loss inside ruling 6912661484) are untouched by the delta.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The delta adds no code.

### ④ Design judgment

S1: closed
N1: closed
N2: closed

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Each new sentence, held against the code at this head:

- Own `readable: false` row beside Modify All (changeset FROM → TO and one-step check; entry `replacement` and `acceptanceCriteria`). "Beside View All that restores every read. Beside Modify All it does not restore a field the same set's own `readable: false` row hides." Right: `viewAllFieldsReadVote` skips a field for which `declaresOwnReadMask` is true, and before 19 only Modify All overrode an own row. The sentence "nothing else is needed for the read" is gone from the entry; the changeset limits it to View All. The remedy (delete the row) is correct.
- Own field row without `editable: true` (changeset, entry `replacement`, `reason` item (2), `acceptanceCriteria`, conversion docblock bullet). Right: `FieldPermissionSchema.editable` is `z.boolean().default(false)`, the merge counts an edit vote only on `entry.editable === true`, and nothing else votes an edit on a field some row names. "With no second set involved" is accurate. The remedy (an explicit `editable: true` row in the set that should edit) is the one grant the merge reads.
- The criteria no longer contradict `reason` item (3); the three places (changeset, entry, conversion docblock) now say the same two own-row cases.
- N1. Both texts now say the authoring funnel skips the conversion because it is retired from the load path, and that the artifact door (`DEFAULT_FLIPS_NOT_REPLAYED_HERE`) and the stored-row seam (`applyConversionsToStoredItem`, through `STORED_ROWS_NOT_REWRITTEN`) refuse it by id. Both names exist at this head and do what is said.
- N2. The comment on `ADMIN_FULL_ACCESS_CAPABILITIES` now says the two record bits cast no field vote from protocol 19 and that `viewAllFields` keeps the administrator's read, "read, never edit: a field another set locks stays locked for a holder of both". That agrees with `buildEffectiveFieldPermissions`: the built-in set has no field rows, so on a field another set's row names it adds a read vote and no edit vote.

No new wrong statement found. One wording note, not graded: "hides the field from the set's holders" is said per set, as it was before the delta; a holder who also holds another set that reads the field still reads it, which is the ordinary union and is stated elsewhere in the entry.
